paper_title: Measuring (a Sufficient) World Model in LLMs A Variance Decomposition   Framework
caption: : Meaningful Variability Share
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled “Meaningful Variability Share” from the paper “Measuring (a Sufficient) World Model in LLMs: A Variance Decomposition Framework,” displays stacked bar plots for four categories—“Health and Nutrition,” “Logistics,” “Personal Finance,” and “Travel and Transportation”—each containing two subgroups labeled “70B llama” and “8B llama.” The vertical axis is scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, representing the proportion of meaningful variability share, while the horizontal axis lists the model categories and their corresponding model sizes. Each bar is divided into two segments: a lower green segment labeled “MVS” and an upper blue segment labeled “1-MVS,” indicating the proportion of variability attributed to the meaningful share and its complement, respectively. In each category, the green “MVS” segment is consistently taller than the blue “1-MVS” segment, with the “70B llama” models generally showing a higher MVS proportion than the “8B llama” models. For example, in “Health and Nutrition,” the “70B llama” bar reaches approximately 0.6 for MVS and 0.4 for 1-MVS, while the “8B llama” bar is approximately 0.4 for MVS and 0.6 for 1-MVS. The bars are arranged in a grouped format, with each category’s two model sizes presented side-by-side, and they are not sorted. The chart visually emphasizes the decomposition of variability share without any additional annotations or highlighting.
